transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called this case conference together because we have a seventh-grade student returning next Monday after missing several weeks of school. As you know, the first ten school days will be managed through a written return-to-school support plan, which I'll sign once we've gathered everyone's input. Before I can sign off on the plan, I need to hear from each of you about your operational constraints. So let's start with the homeroom teacher, the school nurse, and the family liaison -- please share what you need so we can build a solid plan together.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I want to share my operational constraints regarding catch-up work. Yesterday I reviewed the student's missing assignments and counted 18 in total. I've determined that the student can safely complete no more than two catch-up assignments per school day, with mathematics and science handled before the other subjects. I completed this review yesterday but haven't yet entered it in the student support tracker.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share my operational constraints. This morning I reviewed the student's physician clearance, and it specifies that for the first ten school days, the student may attend in person only from 8:30 a.m. through 12:00 p.m. and must be excused from physical education. I should note that I have not yet attached the clearance to the return-plan record, but I will do so promptly.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share my operational constraints. Yesterday I confirmed with the student's caregiver that the student must supervise a younger sibling from 12:30 p.m. through 2:30 p.m., can complete independent schoolwork from 3:00 p.m. through 4:00 p.m., and must use the Oak Street bus stop because the caregiver cannot meet the bus at any other stop. I should note that I have not yet updated the transportation and family-support forms with this information.
transcript.speaker: A4
